newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 26.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Greece is the fourth most popular destination for German tourists, according to recent figures. Greek tourist packages have seen a 6.0 percent increase in sales this year with a similar increase expected next year.

--Veiled threats yesterday from Albanian President Sali Berisha during an election rally in the neighbouring country confirmed feelings that he was trying to undermine the electoral process. Socialist leader Fatos Nano said yesterday he feared violence after the close of polls on Sunday.

--Confusion greeted the first day of nation-wide university entrance exams yesterday when the examiners departed from tradition and selected a recent statement from a member of the Youth Parliament as the topic for the composition exam.
--The father of a young recruit found dead on an Evros army base last week made a pilgrimage yesterday to the site of the murder to lay a wreath and to seek answers.

--Yiannis Spraos, the man behind the recent expert report on how the Greek economy should achieve convergence, says bringing down inflation is the "biggest national issue" and says there should be 'social protection' only to the degree which the economy can tolerate.
--A court in Piraeus has ruled that parking tickets issued in 40 municipalities have no legal basis.
--The 17-year-old who inspired the composition topic in yesterday's exams reveals what he would have written.
--Greece's national basketball team easily bounced its way to victory over Turkey last night, 74-52, in the Eurobasket match in Spain. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
